properties.Name: Genoa
properties.Description: Genoese immigrants settled in Ferry Court due to maritime trade connections, affordable housing, and proximity to work at the waterfront.

properties.Name: Avellino
properties.Description: City that settled slightly apart from the rest of Campania. Similarly settled for affordable housing and proximity to work.

properties.Name: Parma
properties.Description: Affordable housing, close proximity to downtown jobs, and the area's availability of low-rent tenements

properties.Name: Italy
properties.Description: Country of origin for many North End immigrants

properties.Name: West End, Boston
properties.Description: Because of increasing congestion in the North End, wealthier settlers began moving to the West End

properties.Name: Molisan Settlement
properties.Description: Area where Molise region settled.

properties.Name: Jewish Settlement
properties.Description: Location of Jewish immigration from Eastern Europe due to anti-semitism and limited opportunity.

properties.Name: Genoan and Parmigiani Settlement
properties.Description: Historical area near the entrance of the Summer Tunnel. Small courtyard where immigrants from Genoa and Parma settled.

properties.Name: Avellinesi Settlement
properties.Description: Enclave where Avellino diverged from the rest of Campania.

properties.Name: Abruzzesi Settlement
properties.Description: Immigrants from the Abruzzo region settled within the bounds of already existing enclaves of Italian immigrants.

properties.Name: Campanian Settlement
properties.Description: Area where a majority of the Campania region settled. This was the core of North End marketplace activity.

properties.Name: North End, Boston
properties.Description: Neighborhood in north Boston that was the location for Italian immigration during the late 19th and early 10th centuries. A center for cultural and cuisine flourishing that was eventually dubbed Little Italy. This is the MAIN place.

properties.Name: Sicilian Settlement
properties.Description: Settlement near the wharf for access to jobs like fishing and trade

properties.Name: East Boston
properties.Description: Italian populations increasingly crossed the harbor into East Boston. This geographical extension created a unified voting bloc that eventually allowed Italian-American politicians, such as state senator Scollay Langone Jr., to challenge Irish political dominance in a district that tied the North, West, and South Ends together

properties.Name: Abruzzo
properties.Description: Immigration driven by economic hardship, searching for affordable housing.

properties.Name: Molise
properties.Description: Immigrants emerging from a chain of migration and also due to cheap and immediate access to labor.

properties.Name: Campania
properties.Description: Earlier Italian pioneers had already established a foothold there, and immigrants naturally gravitated toward affordable housing near their community and familiar cultural establishments.

properties.Name: Sicily
properties.Description: Especially Sciacca and Castellammare del Golfo; many Sicilians were fishermen, and the North End provided an ideal location for the continuation of this profession with affordable housing.

properties.Name: Romania
properties.Description: Romanian Jewish immigrants came predominantly from the northern and eastern borderlands of the Old Kingdom of Romania

properties.Name: Galicia
properties.Description: Jewish immigrants who listed their country of origin as Austria or Hungary almost exclusively came from a single, specific crown-land: Galicia

properties.Name: Congress Poland
properties.Description: . The Jewish immigrants identifying as "Polish" came primarily from the northeastern districts of Russian-controlled Poland

properties.Name: Lithuania
properties.Description: Lithuanian Jews—culturally known as Litvaks—formed a highly literate, distinct cultural group in Boston

properties.Name: The Pale of Settlement
properties.Description: By far the largest sender of Jewish immigrants to Boston, the Russian Empire restricted its Jewish population to a massive, tightly controlled western border region
